title: Prospective Registry of the West German Pediatric Trial Center (WPSZ) for Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults with Relapsed / Refractory Cancer (WPSZ Registry)
summary:
While the treatment of children, adolescents, and young adults with newly diagnosed cancer or tumors is highly standardized in Germany, this is often not the case when the disease returns (“recurrence,” “recurrent”) or when the disease does not respond to treatment to the expected extent (“refractory”). Thanks to advances in cancer research, in addition to the traditional pillars of therapy—chemotherapy, surgery, and radiation—there are also novel approaches for personalized, innovative therapies based on individual molecular genetic changes in the tumor cells. This means that tumor cells are examined using specialized methods to identify individual changes that distinguish them from healthy body cells (“molecular genetic” or “molecular” diagnostics). These individual changes can then be targeted for treatment with novel (“innovative”) drugs that are precisely tailored to these changes (“personalized” or “targeted” therapy). These therapies and the necessary infrastructure are sometimes only available in pediatric oncology departments at specialized centers, which can make access difficult for patients at other hospitals.
To ensure widespread access to state-of-the-art molecular diagnostics and innovative treatment options, we joined forces several years ago to form the West German Pediatric Study Center (WPSZ).
Through this registry, we aim to enroll all patients treated at a hospital within the WPSZ who have either experienced a relapse of a previous cancer or tumor disease (“recurrence,” “recurred”) or whose initially diagnosed cancer or tumor disease did not respond, or responded inadequately, to the administered therapy. Patients whose cases are discussed in our joint WPSZ Tumor Board due to a blood disorder or other disease should also be included in the registry. Through this data collection, we gain insights into the frequency of recurrent or refractory diseases, the results of molecular tumor analyses, and disease progression.
The data collected in the registry also provides a foundation upon which we can identify additional diagnostic measures (e.g., molecular tumor analyses) and appropriate treatment options during our discussions at the WPSZ Tumor Board. However, the WPSZ registry is used solely for data collection. Decisions regarding diagnosis and treatment, on the other hand, are always made completely independently of participation in the registry, following individual consideration by your treating medical team.
The registry data also helps us prepare for new clinical trials. While strictly adhering to data protection regulations, we would therefore also like to share data with other research groups so that, by working with larger patient cohorts, we can address more scientific questions—for example, regarding new diagnostic and treatment options.

interventions.name: Monitoring of clinical course and quality-of-life-related parameters in children with relapsed or refractory cancer

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
 Diagnosis or suspicion of a relapsed/refractory cancer or
 Diagnosis of a non-cancer / hematological diagnosis if the patient is discussed in the WPSZ tumor board
 Treatment in a hospital of the West German Pediatric Trial Center (WPSZ).
 Written informed consent from parents or legal guardians and/or from the patient if appropriate according to age and status of psycho-intellectual development.
 Enrollment in the PRO/QoL study warrants specific consent at the designated part of the informed consent form for the registry.
Exclusion criteria:
None
